title: GoldenEye 007 Was Made by a Team That Had Never Shipped a Game
hook: GoldenEye 007 was built by around ten people at Rare, most of whom had never shipped a game, and it sold about 8 million copies. This week 007 First Light landed four Game Awards nominations, including Game of the Year. What's your favorite GoldenEye level?
script: Did you know the team that made GoldenEye 007 had mostly never made a game before? In the mid nineties, Rare put a small group of around ten people on a James Bond game for the Nintendo 64. For most of them, it was their first professional game. Director Martin Hollis first planned it as an on-rails shooter, in the style of Sega's arcade hit Virtua Cop. Then the team decided to let Bond move freely through every level. That choice helped define what a console shooter could be. The game took a long time to finish. The GoldenEye film came out in November 1995, and the game did not arrive until August 1997, twenty-one months later. The famous four-player split-screen mode was not even started until the spring of 1997, a few months before release. Programmer Steve Ellis said it really was put in at the last minute. GoldenEye went on to sell about eight million copies, making it the third best-selling game on the Nintendo 64. Bond is back in the headlines this week. On November seventeenth, IO Interactive's 007 First Light picked up four nominations at The Game Awards, including Game of the Year. Patrick Gibson, who plays its young Bond, is up for Best Performance. What is your favorite GoldenEye level? Follow for more gaming history.
